intro: Padded tokens must contribute neither loss nor denominator weight. Compute stable categorical loss only at positions selected by the mask.
task: Return per-token negative log likelihood with zeros at masked positions and its mean over valid positions.
requirements: logits has shape batch-by-time-by-vocabulary. targets and numeric 0/1 mask match batch-by-time. Every target is an integer vocabulary index, even at masked positions. At least one mask entry is one.
Return {"per_token": matrix, "loss": scalar, "count": integer}. Use logsumexp(logits)-target_logit; divide the masked sum by the count of ones, not by batch size or padded area.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Subtract each vocabulary row’s maximum before exponentiating.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Sum the masked losses and divide by the number of valid tokens.

explanation: A token-level mean gives each observed token equal weight even when sequence lengths differ. Dividing by padded area would make loss artificially smaller for batches with more padding.
Stable log-sum-exp avoids overflow and protects confidently wrong predictions from probability underflow. The result remains finite even for large positive and negative logits.
